name: ambilight-never-reads-an-error-page
description:
The first half: an error page is never sampled, and a page that cannot be read leaves the chrome where it was rather than dragging it toward Chromium's grey.

The fixture points at a port nothing listens on, so the tab commits an error page. That page is Chromium's own chrome wearing the site's clothes - sampling it would wash the window the same way for every failed load on the web, which is the opposite of a signal about which page is in front.

The setting is ON here, unlike ambilight-off-leaves-the-space-alone. That is the whole point: this proves the SKIP RULE fires, not that the feature is off.

actions.note: the navigation fails and the error page commits
many sampler ticks, every one of which must decline this page

assertions.label: the-feature-is-actually-on
assertions.desc: THE CONTROL, and this scenario is worthless without it: the event path ran, so the page tint setting really is enabled. Without this, a build with the whole feature disabled would satisfy the assertions below.

assertions.label: the-error-pages-own-white-never-reached-the-chrome
assertions.desc: The skip rule has to gate BOTH doors. Chromium's error page declares theme-color white, so an earlier version of this scenario passed its readback assertion while the declared-tag path washed the chrome white anyway - which is the exact failure the rule exists to prevent. The control above proves the event path ran, so this cannot pass by the sampler being idle.

assertions.label: the-error-page-was-never-read
assertions.desc: The readback declined this page on every tick across four seconds. Its sibling ambilight-reads-both-edges logs this line within half a second on a page that loads.
